Subject: Inquiry: parity and rollback safeguards for migration

Hi Monica / Karthik,

We're nearing internal approval to move a portion of our inference workload off CloudScale to look at Redwood. Procurement flagged two sticky items that could block us: (1) we need a concrete parity and rollback plan in case any latency/regression shows up in pilot, and (2) we want a commercial bridge (credits/discount) to offset migration implementation and egress costs for the first 90 days.

Quick background: our pilot is ~400V100-equivalent token-hours/day across two services (chat + rerank). We can share usage extracts (attached) if helpful. Our timeline is a 3-week pilot window starting the week of Oct 5, with a procurement decision expected Oct 30.

Can Redwood provide:
- a brief term outline for a migration subsidy (caps, timing)
- a technical rollback mechanism (hot standby, routing/fallback SLOs) and any operational costs tied to it
- any guardrails on data retention or audit/logging during rollback

If useful, we can do a 30-minute call this week.

Thanks,
Emma

Hi Emma — really appreciate the clear ask and the export. Congratulations on getting this far in procurement. High level answer below; I attached a short "Parity Safeguard" term sheet for you to share with procurement/legal.

1) Migration subsidy (commercial):
- Offer: one-time onboarding credit equal to 20% of estimated first-quarter usage (applied as USD credits against hosted inference charges). Cap: $150k.
- Duration: credits apply against billings for the first 90 days after go-live.
- Conditions: pilot metrics (latency, error rate) must meet mutually-agreed SLO baselines during pilot.

2) Technical rollback / Safeguard:
- Hot-standby route: we can provision a hybrid routing policy that routes a configurable percentage of traffic to a CloudScale-compatible model variant and also maintain a hot-standby fallback for 72 hours during rollout.
- SLA during rollback window: we commit to <250ms 95th latency for seeded traffic to Redwood-hosted variant; if we miss SLO two days in a row, we will perform an automatic failover to your previous endpoint for up to 72 hours while we remediate.
- Ops cost: standby routing and additional KV cache warm-up incur an uplifted infrastructure surcharge — we estimate ~$5k–8k for the 72-hour standby on your pilot scale; we can absorb 50% of that cost under the migration subsidy above.

3) Data & audit guardrails:
- Logs: we will enable request-level audit logs for the pilot window (retained 90 days) and provide SOC-2-aligned access controls.
- Data retention: by default we do not store prompts longer than session length; any longer-term retention must be agreed in the term sheet.

Next steps: if this aligns, propose a 30-min call Thurs 09/17 at 10am PT to walk the term sheet and get Karthik to validate the rollback sequence. I've looped Neha for legal redlines. Attached: parity-safeguard-term-sheet.pdf.

Best,
Monica Patel

Monica — thanks for the fast turnaround and the term sheet. Couple of clarifying questions before procurement will take it to legal: 

1) On the 20% onboarding credit: is the cap ($150k) negotiable if we can demonstrate a larger first-quarter run rate? Procurement tends to push for a scaled cap tied to committed usage.

2) Standby ops uplift: we appreciate Redwood absorbing 50% — can you confirm the exact dollar figure in the revised term sheet (so legal doesn't have to do a separate cost discovery step)?

3) Automatic failover timing: procurement wants the automatic trigger to be 48 hours of missed SLO (not 2 days with ambiguous boundaries). Can we make that explicit and include a rollback runbook entry that shows the sequence of checks?

4) DocuSign: once we have a revised term sheet with the firm standby cost and the 48-hour automatic-failover language, can you produce a DocuSign link for procurement review?

If you can get a revised term sheet by Monday 21 Sep, we'll route to legal that day. We still aim to start the pilot the week of Oct 5.
